A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLSAE research, with matching authors, core architecture and experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia activation analyses, trained MLSAE experiments, hyperparameter sweeps, reconstruction and downstream-loss measurements, and prompt case studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original standard and tuned-lens MLSAE experiments, conditional variance analyses, larger-model evaluations, and reconstruction, downstream-loss and dictionary-similarity results.

M1.justification: The shared TopK SAE remains, but v2 Section 3.3 introduces a substantive tuned-lens variant: layer-specific pretrained affine transformations precede encoding, inverse transformations follow decoding, and reconstruction losses use transformed coordinates. This relaxes the common-basis restriction through an actual change to the method's input/output procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain Pile-based activation analysis and the indirect-object-identification example prompt. v2 removes the machine-learning and philosophy MMLU prompt cases from v1 Figure 12, modestly narrowing qualitative input coverage. Larger Pythia configurations and changed evaluation splits belong to E3.

E2.justification: v2 adds one closely related comparator, the tuned-lens MLSAE variant, directly compared with standard MLSAEs in Figures 5–6 and 13–14 and Tables 1–2. The literature-based comparisons with single-layer SAEs in Appendix B are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Main aggregate analyses change from the billion-token training dataset to 10 million test tokens, and cosine similarities now use layerwise mean-centered activations. Conditional variance ratios replace the earlier mean layer-distribution SD analysis. MLSAE evaluation extends from Pythia-70m/160m to 410m/1b, and tuned-lens experiments distinguish transformed-space reconstruction metrics from downstream metrics after inversion.

E4.justification: v2 directly tests the shared-basis assumption using tuned lenses, adds residual-norm analysis, and expands model-size and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses using token-conditioned variance measures. Appendix D adds extensive sparsity, Pythia-160m and tuned-lens heatmaps. The dead-latent instability analysis is retained, while the two MMLU case studies are removed.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports SEM error bars for cosine similarity, mean layer SD and MMCS in Figures 1, 4 and 9; v2 omits these SEM descriptions. v2 Table 2 newly reports standard deviations across decoder-vector maximum similarities, which describe dispersion rather than repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version documents repeated training seeds.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5 newly reports aggregate variance fractions of 54–86% and single-token fractions around 1% for standard MLSAEs. Tables 1–2 and additional plots add larger-model and tuned-lens results. The earlier expansion-factor SD results are replaced by variance-ratio findings under changed definitions and sampling, so their differing trends are not same-setting reversals. MMLU result entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's pooled-activation layer distribution with an explicit conditional construction over tokens, latents and layers, defines variance ratios, and develops their total-variance decomposition in Appendix C. Section 3.3 derives the tuned-lens inverse. Section 3.2 also corrects the auxiliary-loss residual from a scalar squared norm to x - x_hat; this correction alone does not establish an implementation change.

C1.justification: v2 adds the central quantitative claim of an approximately two-order-of-magnitude aggregate-versus-token variance gap and claims qualitative persistence after tuned-lens transformations. It replaces v1's emphasis on expansion-factor robustness with increasing aggregate sharing under the new variance measure, and strengthens the conclusion that representation drift obstructs SAE-based interpretation.

C2.justification: v1 leaves basis relaxation and larger-model generalization as future work; v2 interprets experiments addressing both and discusses the limited effect of tuned-lens alignment. Its discussion adds reconstruction-evaluation and changing-context arguments against concatenating layers, while the conclusion newly emphasizes representation drift as an obstacle to identifying computational variables.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the specific Pile dataset source, identifies the tuned-lens implementation and its residual connection, explains precomputing inverse transformations, and notes unavailable pretrained lenses for Pythia-1b. Appendix A's batching, preprocessing, initialization and optimizer details are largely unchanged, as is access to the authors' code.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning around logit/tuned lenses and iterative inference, plus references concerning representation drift, nonlinear features and uncertain SAE advantages in causal analysis. The MMLU reference disappears with its examples. The central novelty positioning—a single SAE shared across residual-stream layers—remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary are substantially rewritten. Existing method explanations are reorganized into Setup and Training subsections, results gain a thematic subsection structure, and the rewritten Discussion distinguishes data-stacked and feature-stacked approaches. A separate Conclusion and organized mathematical and heatmap appendices substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds variance-ratio bar charts, residual-norm and tuned-lens comparison plots, and two numerical tables. Main heatmaps expand to additional models, appendix evaluation figures combine model-specific panels, and sweep axes change from latent counts to expansion factors. The MMLU figure is removed, while retained figures are reorganized and redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central finding: v1's largely illustrative aggregate-versus-prompt contrast gains explicit token-conditioned quantification on test data, while tuned-lens and larger-model experiments address limitations previously left open. Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix C make the evidence more systematic and interpretable. These gains outweigh the loss of two prompt cases and less explicit SEM reporting; they do not depend on treating transformed-space reconstruction scores as directly comparable performance improvements.
